newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin boasts success in defusing Belarus crisis.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin boasts success in defusing Belarus crisis.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin, speaking with feeling in his first television interview at the Barvikha sanatorium where he moved on Friday, claimed success in defusing a crisis in neighbouring Belarus.
"I consider this to be a big victory," said Yeltsin, who appears to have lost a lot of weight after a quintuple heart bypass operation on November 5. "The crisis is over."

Yeltsin, who left hospital earlier on Friday and moved to his favoured Barvikha rest home outside Moscow, said a stand-off between Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko and parliament over a referendum due on Sunday could have led to clashes.

"As a friendly country and as a member of the (Russia-Belarus) community we could not allow Belarus to split. As the president of Russia I could not allow that. That is why we took all the measures we could to find a compromise."

Yeltsin, sitting in an armchair, appeared to be talking at ease and was in an obviously better form than in months before his operation when his brief television appearences were heavily edited and when he found it difficult to speak.

Russia and Belarus signed an agreement in April to form a loose alliance. Yeltsin spoke to Lukashenko by telephone on Thursday and Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin flew to Minsk later that day.
After all-night talks Lukashenko agreed on Friday that a planned Sunday referendum on expanding his powers should not be legally binding.
His opponents in parliament, who accuse him of dictatorial ambitions, in turn agreed to drop impeachment proceedings against him.

But the compromise document faced heated debate in parliament and Lukashenko has called on the deputies to approve the accord by a two-thirds majority by 6 p.m. (1600 GMT) with no amendments or conditions attached.
